headline: Two oil tankers disabled by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz, says IRGC
summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers were disabled by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran has also warned that military bases in Europe could be targeted in a new US war.
why: Hormuz carries roughly a fifth of global oil; disruption feeds straight into Pakistan's fuel import bill.
credit: JMSDF / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0 (file photo)

headline: At COP31, PM Shehbaz calls for grant-based climate finance for vulnerable countries
summary: Speaking in Antalya, the prime minister said climate-vulnerable nations need timely support that does not deepen their debt, and pressed for stronger resilience and adaptation funds.
why: Loss-and-damage and debt-free adaptation finance are recurring essay and Current Affairs themes.
credit: Royd Moor Wind Farm, Flickr, CC BY 2.0

headline: Punjab CM says rivers hold significant evidence of placer gold
summary: At the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum in Islamabad, Maryam Nawaz pointed to Mianwali and Attock, as provinces pitched mining opportunities to domestic and foreign investors.
why: Mineral wealth and export diversification tie into Pakistan's economic recovery debate.

headline: Pakistan's quiet solar revolution: 22GW of rooftop panels in two years
summary: Addressing a COP31 clean-energy dialogue, PM Shehbaz Sharif said ordinary citizens added nearly 22 gigawatts of rooftop solar in just two years, seeking affordable power and a cleaner, more predictable future.
why: A ready-made example for essays on energy security, circular debt and the clean-energy transition.

headline: China accuses US of using spy claims to justify a technology blockade
summary: Beijing's foreign ministry said Washington is fabricating 'spy' narratives as a pretext for restricting China's access to advanced technology, as the US-China chip rivalry deepens.
why: US-China tech rivalry shapes global supply chains and the strategic choices facing Pakistan.

headline: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough
summary: Talks in Abu Dhabi centred on Europe's future security framework. US envoys were due to meet Presidents Putin and Zelensky on Thursday.
